keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1540-1791 (Cliopatria's row starts in 1792): 'traditionally credited with founding Imerina in 1540' (Andriamanelo). The page gives the capitals (Alasora, Ambohidrabiby, Ambohimanga, Antananarivo) and no boundaries, area or division of the kingdom; a 30 km circle round Antananarivo holds all four (the researcher's reading), and the kingdom was reunited by Andrianampoinimerina from 1787.

1792-1795, 67,330 km2 (261 cells, 11.5 per cent of the island; 127 of the 173 cells of the gazetteer's 'Imerina' circle). Andrianampoinimerina took the throne in 1787, conquered Antananarivo in 1793 and by 1795 had 'gained the allegiance and submission of all the territories' that had formed Imerina at its largest. The page gives no boundary or area; the Merina Kingdom page has no infobox area.

1796-1802, 85,401 km2 (+69 cells to the south, lat -21.2 to -19.1: the northern Betsileo and Antsirabe country). The page dates no southern conquest ('from around 1800' the effort to unite the island's ethnic groups; Betsileo named among the territories absorbed). Unverified.

1803-1810, 112,887 km2 (+107 cells to the east, lon 47.8-48.9: Sihanaka and Bezanozano country). The page names the Sihanaka and the Bezanozano among the absorbed territories without dates. Unverified.

1811-1813, back to the 1792 shape (67,330 km2): a contraction of 175 cells. The Radama I page says only that after his 1810 accession 'rebellions followed' and the campaigns 'included completing the pacification of the Betsileo kingdom'; it names no lost land. The shape stands, unverified; it may be a Cliopatria artefact.
1814-1819, 112,887 km2, the 1803 shape again (+175 cells), consistent with the pacification of the Betsileo.

keyframe_review.note: 1820-1821, 173,288 km2. The shape already reaches Antsiranana (5 cells, the north tip) in 1820, although the page puts the posts at Vohemar and Diego Suarez in 1824; it lacks Toamasina (1817). Toamasina is added; the early north tip is left, as a polygon rather than a post (unverified).

keyframe_review.note: 1822-1823, 244,722 km2 (+273 cells down the east and south-east, lat -22.7 to -14.0). The page dates 'westward campaigns into Menabe in 1820, 1821 and 1822' and 'military expeditions along the northeast coast' in 1823; Toamasina (1817) is added to the shape.

1824, 369,241 km2 (+434 cells in the west, lon 43.5 to 48.9). Agrees with the page: 'By 1824, the Merina captured the port of Mahajanga' and the Menabe campaigns of 1820-1822 (Morondava is inside the shape).

1825-1833, 374,728 km2 (60.8 per cent of the island's cells). +20 cells at Fort Dauphin: 'In 1825 military posts were established in the southeastern coastal towns of Farafangana and Fort Dauphin.' The page: 'Radama united two thirds of the island under Merina rule'; 'the areas retaining independence included most of Bara country, Mahafaly and Antandroy in the south, northern Menabe and Ambongo in the west'.

1834-1839, 397,202 km2 (+97 cells in the south-west, lat -24.7 to -20.7). Unverified: the Ranavalona I page has no conquests, reconquests or losses of land ('Not on the page'); it says only that she wished 'to extend her realm over the entire island'.

1840-1894, 426,716 km2 (69.5 per cent of the island's cells; +109 cells in the west, lat -20 to -16). Unverified for 1840: the page dates no extension. It holds to 1884: Antsiranana is ceded in December 1885 (new keyframe 1885). Close to Radama's 'two thirds' of the island, but the shape takes in the Ambongo country the Radama page lists as independent in 1828.

keyframe_review.note: 1895-1897, the 1840 shape. The French took Toamasina on 12 December 1894 and entered Antananarivo on 1 October 1895; 'put under French protection in 1896', the monarchy ended in 1897. Antsiranana stays French.

ledger.note: c. 1540: Andriamanelo is traditionally credited with founding Imerina on the central highlands. 'who is traditionally credited with founding Imerina in 1540.' The page gives no extent; the circle round Antananarivo is the researcher's reading of the capitals it names.
1793: Andrianampoinimerina conquers Antananarivo. 'Andrianampoinimerina conquered Antananarivo in 1793.' He took the throne at Ambohimanga in 1787 after exiling his uncle Andrianjafy.
1794: the capital returns to Antananarivo. 'He shifted the kingdom's political capital back to Antananarivo in 1794.' (from Ambohimanga)

1811: land lost to rebels at Radama's accession. Cliopatria's shape shrinks by 175 cells for 1811-1813; the Radama I page says only that after he succeeded in 1810 'rebellions followed' (page silent on any land). Counterpart 'nobody' for the rebel-held land.
1814: the lost land is regained. The campaigns after the accession 'included completing the pacification of the Betsileo kingdom'; the year is the shape's (page silent).

region.text: the port town of Toamasina (Tamatave) and its military post

ledger.note: 1817: Radama I takes Toamasina. 'Radama's territorial expansion began in 1817 with a campaign to the eastern port town of Toamasina'; he set up a military post there.

23 October 1817: the Anglo-Merina treaty recognises Radama as 'King of Madagascar'. 'On 23 October 1817, Radama signed a treaty negotiated by former military general James Hastie'; Britain recognised him in exchange for 'horses, uniforms and a pledge to abandon the export of slaves'. The Merina Kingdom is also called the Kingdom of Madagascar from here.

1820: the Merina campaign into Menabe. 'This was followed by a series of westward campaigns into Menabe in 1820, 1821 and 1822.' The page does not say what was held; northern Menabe was independent at Radama's death.
1822: the last Menabe campaign. The shape of 1824 (Morondava inside) shows the west taken.

notes:
Start: the Merina Kingdom page gives 'founding Imerina in 1540' (Andriamanelo); Cliopatria's row starts in 1792, so 1540-1791 is a new keyframe with a small circle round Antananarivo (no page gives an extent or the division of Imerina before Andrianampoinimerina, which the unification page implies). The extent before 1787 should be checked by a gap-filler (a page on Imerina's history). Areas: the Merina Kingdom page has no infobox area, so the 'two thirds of the island' of the Radama I page is the check: the 1825-1833 shape covers 60.8 per cent of the island's land cells, the 1840 shape 69.5 per cent.

Cliopatria's dates differ from the pages: Toamasina 1817 (page) against 1824 (shape; corrected by new keyframe 1817 and adjusts to 1820 and 1822); the north tip (Antsiranana) is in the 1820 shape but the posts at Vohemar and Diego Suarez are of 1824; the Menabe campaigns 1820-1822 against the west in 1824. The 1811-1813 contraction has only the Radama page's 'rebellions followed'. The steps of 1796 and 1803 (Betsileo, Sihanaka, Bezanozano) have no year on the pages. The 1834 and 1840 steps (south-west and west) have no page at all (the Ranavalona I page is silent on territory).

Disagreements between pages: Franco-Hova hostilities 1882 (Merina Kingdom page) or 1883; the protectorate 1882-1897 in the infobox against 1896 in the text, and 1885 for foreign policy; the French invasion '1883' and '1894' in different passages; Ambohimanga as capital 'around 1610' against Andrianjaka's reign 1612-1630 and the Antananarivo compound.

States needing a dossier from the af-07-x batch: Betsimisaraka Kingdom (counterpart of the 1817 Toamasina gain), the Sakalava kingdoms of Menabe and Boina, the Antankarana and the Antalaotra, Antanosy, Antesaka and the Betsileo kingdoms (Cliopatria lacks all of them). French Africa (Cliopatria row 1846-1957) has no shape in Madagascar before 1898, so the Antsiranana loss (1885) and the war zones of 1894-1895 are counterparts without a drawn French shape. Region names the gazetteer lacks: Vohemar and Fort Dauphin (Tôlanaro resolves), the Tanala country (a coordinate radius is used).
